Rs2xIFtlFHI.title: Listening to the Divine: At-Tawbah 38-43
Rs2xIFtlFHI.one_line: Tabuk and the cave: mobilize whatever you have, Allah needs no one, courage at your lowest point, and no insurance policy with God.
Rs2xIFtlFHI.summary: A year-end khutbah on At-Tawbah 38-42, the verses revealed when the Prophet called the people out to Tabuk. He opens with a warning about Bill C-9, which he fears could make quoting Quranic verses prosecutable and which he says targets Muslims without consultation with imams, and urges people to write to their MPs. Tabuk came at the worst time, a thousand kilometres north in August when exhausted people needed their harvest, and for once the Prophet named the destination openly; the mixed response drew the rebuke of 9:38. He reads infiru as mobilize whatever you have, physician, lawyer or programmer, and hears the heaviness of iththaqaltum in the word itself. Allah needs no one; you mobilize for your own record. Then 9:40 takes him to the hijrah: perfectly planned, yet the pursuers reached the very cave, and the Prophet said not do not fear but do not be sad, because they had done everything they could and Allah was with them. The moment that defines you is at the bottom of the valley, still standing. The second khutbah on 9:41-42 condemns those who would come for a short profitable trip but not for a lifetime of effort: there is no insurance policy with Allah, go all in, and may the new year bring that courage.

outline.heading: Opening
Recitation of the passage
outline.gist: He recites At-Tawbah 38 to 40, from clinging heavily to the earth to the word of Allah being highest.

outline.heading: Bill C-9 and the freedom to quote the Quran
outline.gist: Listen to Allah, who began the conversation. He chose these verses fearing the government may soon bar him from quoting them: the bill could label Quranic words as prohibited speech, will be used on Muslims alone, and was advanced without consulting the community or its imams, another attempt to restrict their liberty.

outline.heading: Every end is a beginning
outline.gist: The verses suit the end of the year, more properly the hijri year; noticing that something has ended invites reflection on what to do better with the days, months or whatever time remains.

outline.heading: Tabuk: a second round with the Romans
outline.gist: The first round at Mu'tah ended in a strategic retreat counted as a victory; now the emperor in the north had massed troops and allies, and the Prophet chose to meet them in the north rather than let them march toward Madinah.

outline.heading: The worst possible timing
outline.gist: Like a Friday when weather and work make you wonder whether to come, and you would be excused; but this was a matter of the security of the deen and the nation.

outline.heading: He always concealed his destination
outline.gist: The Prophet never revealed where he was heading, even misdirecting his own army: positioned east, scouts sent west, while he was going south all along, so no one would worry and no secret could leak.

outline.heading: Except Tabuk: the destination named openly
outline.gist: A thousand kilometres north in mid-August, when people were poor, sick and exhausted and needed the dates on their trees; the response was mixed and the Quran answered almost immediately.

outline.heading: Infiru: mobilize whatever you have
outline.gist: To go forth means get up and move with whatever you do: physician, lawyer, teacher, driver, the programmer with his laptop. Bring what you know how to do.

outline.heading: The heaviness of clinging to the earth
outline.gist: Iththaqaltum carries its heaviness in its very sound, audible even to non-Arabic speakers. When the call says all hands on deck tomorrow morning, suddenly your back hurts and your body cannot lift off the ground.

outline.heading: Satisfied with this life over the next?
outline.gist: Clinging to the earth means something of this world attracts you more than the Hereafter; yet the enjoyment of this life, set against the next, is little.

outline.heading: He will replace you; you harm Him nothing
outline.gist: If you do not go forth He will punish you and bring another people, and you will not harm Him at all. You do this for you; no one does Allah a favour by mobilizing.

outline.heading: Allah is not begging
outline.gist: Whenever He asks for something heavy He reminds you not to imagine He needs you; you bear the consequences of your choice either way, and He is giving you an opportunity to put on your record for the Day of Judgment.

outline.heading: Allah aided him when none of you were there
outline.gist: If you do not support him, Allah already did, many times, when the disbelievers drove him out, the second of two in the cave with Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, telling him do not be sad.

outline.heading: Had he been caught, the story would have ended
outline.gist: There was not yet enough momentum and much of the revelation had not come; had the hijrah failed there would have been no later victories or conquests.

outline.heading: The moment that matters most
outline.gist: It is not the hilltop but the bottom of the valley, when you are still on your feet, still standing and still mobilizing, though you cannot see any light at the end of the tunnel.

outline.heading: The hijrah planned to perfection
outline.gist: Your legacy is how you behaved at your lowest. The camels waited outside, he left at midnight with Ali in his bed after weeks of sleeping there at that hour, a shepherd's flock covered the tracks, they went south for three days to a remote cave and sent the camels away.

outline.heading: They reached the very cave
outline.gist: Against all odds, with no one knowing where they went, the pursuers found not the mountain or the area but the cave itself, while the two hid in a smaller hollow inside.

outline.heading: Not do not fear, but do not be sad
outline.gist: Hearing Abu Jahl and the others on the steps, they thought it was over. The Prophet did not tell Abu Bakr not to be afraid, because he did not know what would happen next; the beauty of the story is his courage.

outline.heading: We did everything we could; Allah is with us
outline.gist: Why be sad? If death comes we die on our feet doing what we were asked, with Allah pleased with us; there was no shortcoming in the plan. All the pursuers had to do was look down and see his feet.

outline.heading: The pursuers who never looked down
outline.gist: Seven or eight of them stood around and on top of the cave, one close enough to see through a small hole, yet no one looked; he imagines them later blaming each other for not checking.

outline.heading: Tranquility and unseen soldiers
outline.gist: Allah sent down His tranquility and supported him with soldiers they did not see, made the word of the disbelievers lowest and His own word the highest.

outline.heading: Interlude
A near gain and a short journey
outline.gist: Go forth light or heavy and strive with wealth and life. Had it been a quick profit a hundred kilometres away they would have come; the issue was the effort. Such people are there when it is easy but not when it takes a lifetime.

outline.heading: False oaths, and the courage to go all in
outline.gist: They swear they would have come if they could, destroying themselves, and Allah knows they lie. Do not be in for small efforts and out for big ones; mobilize all you have, which takes courage.

outline.heading: No insurance policy with Allah
outline.gist: People spread their bets like investors diversifying stocks, but with Allah there is no hedge: go all in, let the bricks fall where they may, and may the new year bring the courage he showed in the cave.

outline.heading: He decides how the story is told
outline.gist: Do not be sad, we did everything we could; if this is the end we die standing and courageous. My job is to mobilize with everything I have; He decides how the story is told, and I decide only what I did.

outline.heading: Outro

I2uAbfrjsKE.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Qiyamah, Part 1: Verses 1-5
I2uAbfrjsKE.one_line: Al-Qiyamah as dawah by reason: oaths by the Day stands are taken and by the self-blaming conscience, and man's real motive for denial.
I2uAbfrjsKE.summary: The sheikh places Al-Qiyamah in his reading of Juz Tabarak as a cluster on representing Islam. Its last three surahs model three ways of calling people: reason, desire for reward, and fear of punishment. Reason comes first because it puts a person on the track, while emotion keeps him there; emotion without reason, in dawah as in marriage, is manipulation. The first oath is by Yawm al-Qiyamah, which he reads as the Day stands are taken. Now Allah leaves us to our choices, but then He will stand toward each person according to the stands they took, with no appeal and no extension; certainty that arrives then is like shouting the answer after handing in the exam, while small changes made now count enormously. The second oath is by the self-blaming soul, the conscience Allah installs in everyone, which weakens when the spirit is starved. Parents must help children develop it rather than rely only on reward and punishment. Verses 3 and 4 answer doubt about resurrection with logic: the One who created you from nothing will rebuild you down to your fingerprints. Verse 5 exposes the real motive: people want a future of blame-free indulgence. He asks listeners to keep asking themselves why they want what they want.

outline.heading: Juz Tabarak as a cluster on representation
outline.gist: The first four surahs cover the knowledge, ethics, spirituality and behaviour needed to represent the deen; Nuh and Al-Jinn give an example of dawah that did not work out and one that did.

outline.heading: What you take from Islam and what you give
outline.gist: Al-Muzzammil and Al-Muddaththir, among the earliest revelations, describe what Islam gives you inwardly (night prayer, Quran, closeness to Allah) and what you carry out to the world.

outline.heading: Three ways to call people: reason, reward, fear
outline.gist: The cluster's last three surahs model dawah through intellect, through desire for reward, and through reverence and fear of punishment. Al-Qiyamah is the first, built on reason.

outline.heading: Reason speaks to the higher spirit
outline.gist: Reason is the most intimate and impactful way. A marriage proposal is a reasoned commitment to protect and provide, the foundation for the emotions that follow.

outline.heading: Emotion without reason is manipulation
outline.gist: Islam forbids stirring emotions in a relationship not grounded in a clear commitment. Likewise, dawah full of talk of Paradise and Hell to someone who does not know who God is burns out quickly.

outline.heading: Reason puts you on the track, emotion keeps you there
outline.gist: Critical thinking chooses the right track; reward and punishment supply the motivation not to fall off it.

outline.heading: Driving: reason plus penalties
outline.gist: You drive by reason, but penalties stop you running red lights. Many leave the centre in tears from the Quran and then race down Gainsborough as if it were a Formula One track.

outline.heading: Muslims who drive like warriors
outline.gist: Lost licences and impounded cars are common across the community. A man once sped past him as a pedestrian near Victoria Hospital without recognizing him; we do not carry our ethics onto the road.

outline.heading: A body without wings can still get somewhere
outline.gist: Dawah missing any of the three is incomplete, but reason is the body and the other two are wings. That is why Al-Qiyamah, the shortest and most profound of the three, comes first.

outline.heading: Recitation of the opening verses
outline.gist: All the surahs of this cluster are Meccan, with at most a verse or two that some scholars place in Medina. He recites the passage.

outline.heading: Two hamzas in a row
outline.gist: A tajweed note: some recitations merge consecutive hamzas, but in ours each must be pronounced clearly, which takes effort from the throat.

outline.heading: La uqsimu: I need not swear, but I will
outline.gist: The negation before the oath is an Arabic figure of speech that emphasizes the oath: I do not need to swear to convince you, yet I swear.

outline.heading: From qum to Qiyamah
outline.gist: The first commands of Al-Muzzammil and Al-Muddaththir were to stand: for yourself, then for the world. Al-Qiyamah comes from the same root.

outline.heading: The Day stands are taken
outline.gist: Qiyamah can mean a long standing, but he prefers the Day a stand is taken about each of us. Now Allah leaves us to our choices and does not strike down oppressors at once.

outline.heading: History tries to judge people too
outline.gist: We study historical figures to decide what stand to take on them: agreed on Hitler, divided on others. On that Day the final stand will be clear.

outline.heading: He will stand toward you as you stood toward Him
outline.gist: Allah's judgment of you rests on the stands you took. For now everything is fluid; no one knows their rank.

outline.heading: No appeal and no extension
outline.gist: On that Day everything halts and Allah clarifies what was hidden for all hundred billion humans who have lived. Having no options, no appeal and no way to remove a record is what makes it so hard.

outline.heading: No rewriting your legacy
outline.gist: In this life even someone who supported genocide, apartheid and Zionism for decades can reverse his stand in his final year. On that Day what you did is what you did.

outline.heading: The name of the Day that speaks to reason
outline.gist: Of over sixteen names for the Day, most stir fear; Al-Qiyamah describes its reality. Those saved will feel they barely made it, too humbled to look down on anyone.

outline.heading: Your fate is in your hands now
outline.gist: The most painful part of that Day is being unable to change your fate, while today every choice shapes it and you can change your mind about anything.

outline.heading: Everyone will believe on that Day
outline.gist: Every bigotry and bad habit will vanish, and the worst person will have more certainty than the most pious person alive today, but it will no longer count.

outline.heading: The book is closed
outline.gist: In this world hardships that change you count toward your destiny. Punishment that cleanses sin on that Day is a separate matter; a change of belief there counts for nothing.

outline.heading: Shouting the answer after handing in the exam
outline.gist: Seeing good people on that Day and wishing you had lived like them is like calling out the right answer after submitting your paper.

outline.heading: Small changes now count colossally
outline.gist: Unseen changes made today can save you, while the greatest show of repentance on that Day adds up to nothing. Take the stand now.

outline.heading: The second oath: the self-blaming soul
outline.gist: The worldly nafs wants food, sex, status and control for itself; the spirit carries empathy and love.

outline.heading: A starved spirit leaves a dead conscience
outline.gist: Some can kill and steal without losing sleep; others stay upset with themselves long after a mistake, because their spirit is strong.

outline.heading: It blames itself, not others
outline.gist: A conscience that blames others is worthless. The spirit came from Allah and starves without what connects to Him, just as the body starves without food.

outline.heading: An internal motive installed in everyone
outline.gist: Before any reward or punishment, Allah pre-programmed a conscience that tells right from wrong without external sources. Polygraphs work because the body hates lying; those who beat them have killed it.

outline.heading: The child behind the couch with a cookie
outline.gist: Watching a five-year-old caught breaking a rule struggle over whether to lie shows the conscience at work. External rules alone run out.

outline.heading: Raise children with an inner compass
outline.gist: The conscience grows with knowledge, clarity, good company and examples. Children ruled only by parental reward and punishment will not make it once the parent is gone, whatever their age.

outline.heading: We love to silence the nag
outline.gist: The conscience nags and we want it quiet. A young person doing wrong without enjoying it while everyone else seems to still has a living conscience.

outline.heading: When a child has no conscience
outline.gist: Once it is dead, return takes years if it comes at all. After decades with youth he can spot a child who feels no blame, cannot fix that in a few hours at the masjid, and must protect others.

outline.heading: Two oaths anchored in reason
outline.gist: Allah never swears idly. Both oaths, by a Day described purely by its logic and by the reasoning, choosing part of the human, prepare for what follows; the answer to the oath is left unstated.

outline.heading: Does man think We will not gather his bones?
outline.gist: The surah delays the oath's answer and asks whether man thinks reassembling his bones is beyond his Creator.

outline.heading: Taswiyah: rebuilding in perfect balance
outline.gist: Nusawwiya means making something exactly balanced, like an equation or a settlement in court.

outline.heading: Down to the fingerprint
outline.gist: Banan is the fingertip: among a hundred billion people no two fingerprints match, and Allah will restore each one exactly, not a rough Frankenstein assembly.

outline.heading: An argument of basic logic
outline.gist: Not fear or desire but logic: if He created you from nothing, why is bringing you back hard to grasp? You will find no difference between how you remember yourself and how you rise.

outline.heading: Bal: that is not the real problem
outline.gist: Bal denies what came before and affirms what follows: people can easily accept that their Creator can reassemble them.

outline.heading: Why not use the system inside you?
outline.gist: The real question is why people do not live as if a stand will be taken about them. Consulted before every word and act, the conscience would guide them right every time.

outline.heading: Wanting a blame-free future
outline.gist: Man wants to commit fujur ahead of him, breaking Allah's law to scratch every itch, with no conscience and no day of judgment to answer to.

outline.heading: A story to excuse desire
outline.gist: Rules feel tiring when young and healthy, so people build a rationale that lets them indulge blame-free; killing the conscience requires reasoning with it.

outline.heading: The conscience keeps nagging
outline.gist: Even with the best excuse for zina, drink or drugs, people feel awful afterwards; some take until their sixties or seventies to silence it and waste wealth while others die.

outline.heading: Dawah that explains your own motives
outline.gist: The following verses lay out how the human reasons. Understanding why you feel what you feel lets you deal with it maturely.

outline.heading: Ask why, then ask why again
outline.gist: Keep asking why you want something until the shameful root appears. The surah builds its case by reason toward living with purpose rather than being left aimless.

17:23.ar: ۞وَقَضَىٰ رَبُّكَ أَلَّا تَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِيَّاهُ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۚ إِمَّا يَبۡلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلۡكِبَرَ أَحَدُهُمَآ أَوۡ كِلَاهُمَا فَلَا تَقُل لَّهُمَآ أُفࣲّ وَلَا تَنۡهَرۡهُمَا وَقُل لَّهُمَا قَوۡلࣰ ا كَرِيمࣰ ا
17:23.en: And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment. Whether one or both of them reach old age [while] with you, say not to them [so much as], "uff," and do not repel them but speak to them a noble word

17:24.ar: وَٱخۡفِضۡ لَهُمَا جَنَاحَ ٱلذُّلِّ مِنَ ٱلرَّحۡمَةِ وَقُل رَّبِّ ٱرۡحَمۡهُمَا كَمَا رَبَّيَانِي صَغِيرࣰ ا
17:24.en: And lower to them the wing of humility out of mercy and say, "My Lord, have mercy upon them as they brought me up [when I was] small

17:25.ar: رَّبُّكُمۡ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَا فِي نُفُوسِكُمۡۚ إِن تَكُونُواْ صَٰلِحِينَ فَإِنَّهُۥ كَانَ لِلۡأَوَّٰبِينَ غَفُورࣰ ا
17:25.en: Your Lord is most knowing of what is within yourselves. If you should be righteous [in intention] - then indeed He is ever, to the often returning [to Him], Forgiving

17:26.ar: وَءَاتِ ذَا ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ حَقَّهُۥ وَٱلۡمِسۡكِينَ وَٱبۡنَ ٱلسَّبِيلِ وَلَا تُبَذِّرۡ تَبۡذِيرًا
17:26.en: And give the relative his right, and [also] the poor and the traveler, and do not spend wastefully

17:27.ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡمُبَذِّرِينَ كَانُوٓاْ إِخۡوَٰنَ ٱلشَّيَٰطِينِۖ وَكَانَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لِرَبِّهِۦ كَفُورࣰ ا
17:27.en: Indeed, the wasteful are brothers of the devils, and ever has Satan been to his Lord ungrateful

17:28.ar: وَإِمَّا تُعۡرِضَنَّ عَنۡهُمُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ رَحۡمَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكَ تَرۡجُوهَا فَقُل لَّهُمۡ قَوۡلࣰ ا مَّيۡسُورࣰ ا
17:28.en: And if you [must] turn away from the needy awaiting mercy from your Lord which you expect, then speak to them a gentle word

17:29.ar: وَلَا تَجۡعَلۡ يَدَكَ مَغۡلُولَةً إِلَىٰ عُنُقِكَ وَلَا تَبۡسُطۡهَا كُلَّ ٱلۡبَسۡطِ فَتَقۡعُدَ مَلُومࣰ ا مَّحۡسُورًا
17:29.en: And do not make your hand [as] chained to your neck or extend it completely and [thereby] become blamed and insolvent

17:30.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكَ يَبۡسُطُ ٱلرِّزۡقَ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَقۡدِرُۚ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ بِعِبَادِهِۦ خَبِيرَۢا بَصِيرࣰ ا
17:30.en: Indeed, your Lord extends provision for whom He wills and restricts [it]. Indeed He is ever, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing

6:151.ar: ۞قُلۡ تَعَالَوۡاْ أَتۡلُ مَا حَرَّمَ رَبُّكُمۡ عَلَيۡكُمۡۖ أَلَّا تُشۡرِكُواْ بِهِۦ شَيۡـࣰٔ اۖ وَبِٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ إِحۡسَٰنࣰ اۖ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُوٓاْ أَوۡلَٰدَكُم مِّنۡ إِمۡلَٰقࣲ نَّحۡنُ نَرۡزُقُكُمۡ وَإِيَّاهُمۡۖ وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ ٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ مَا ظَهَرَ مِنۡهَا وَمَا بَطَنَۖ وَلَا تَقۡتُلُواْ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَعۡقِلُونَ
6:151.en: Say, "Come, I will recite what your Lord has prohibited to you. [He commands] that you not associate anything with Him, and to parents, good treatment, and do not kill your children out of poverty; We will provide for you and them. And do not approach immoralities - what is apparent of them and what is concealed. And do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden [to be killed] except by [legal] right. This has He instructed you that you may use reason

6:152.ar: وَلَا تَقۡرَبُواْ مَالَ ٱلۡيَتِيمِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ أَشُدَّهُۥۚ وَأَوۡفُواْ ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَٱلۡمِيزَانَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِۖ لَا نُكَلِّفُ نَفۡسًا إِلَّا وُسۡعَهَاۖ وَإِذَا قُلۡتُمۡ فَٱعۡدِلُواْ وَلَوۡ كَانَ ذَا قُرۡبَىٰۖ وَبِعَهۡدِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡفُواْۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
6:152.en: And do not approach the orphan's property except in a way that is best until he reaches maturity. And give full measure and weight in justice. We do not charge any soul except [with that within] its capacity. And when you testify, be just, even if [it concerns] a near relative. And the covenant of Allah fulfill. This has He instructed you that you may remember

6:153.ar: وَأَنَّ هَٰذَا صِرَٰطِي مُسۡتَقِيمࣰ ا فَٱتَّبِعُوهُۖ وَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلسُّبُلَ فَتَفَرَّقَ بِكُمۡ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ وَصَّىٰكُم بِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
6:153.en: And, [moreover], this is My path, which is straight, so follow it; and do not follow [other] ways, for you will be separated from His way. This has He instructed you that you may become righteous

FIYkWMoPSmY.title: Listening to the Divine: Al-Isra 23-39
FIYkWMoPSmY.one_line: The ten commandments of the Quran: worship Allah alone, excellence to parents, rights in wealth; and keep Gaza alive when the news cools.
FIYkWMoPSmY.summary: An early khutbah in his Listening to the Divine series on Al-Isra 23-39, the passage scholars call the ten commandments of the Quran. He sets out the premise: a khutbah exists only to bring Allah's own words closer to the listener, and since Allah spoke first, every dua is a reply; the question is whether you listened. Before the verses he raises a concern he has voiced before: the real test of a cause is how people behave once it cools in the public eye. When the bombing stops, Gaza drops out of Muslim conversation within weeks while Sudan starves. Individual breaks from the news are healthy, but the ummah's attention must not lapse, and he charges young Muslims with keeping just causes alive, reminding them that the Prophet died thirty years before the conquests he foretold and that founders rarely see their harvest. He then reads 17:23-30 slowly: worship for Allah alone, excellence to parents with not even the sound uff, the noble word, the wing of humility, the rights of relatives, the needy and the stranded in wealth that is not yours, the wasteful as siblings of the devils, and the balance between a tight fist and an open hand. Out of time, he asks them to live as though these verses were all the Quran they had.

outline.heading: Opening
Bringing Allah's words closer
outline.gist: Speakers get carried away with their own explanations, but the only purpose of the minbar is to bring the Quran closer to the listener's consciousness; for the coming weeks he will take powerful passages people already know.

outline.heading: He spoke first; your dua is a reply
outline.gist: Listen for the words Allah chose, not the rhythm or the beautiful voice. Allah does not answer back when you speak because He already spoke; did you listen to Him, or do you only want Him to listen to you and offer a compromise?

outline.heading: The real test of a cause
outline.gist: How people behave once a cause cools down in the public eye is the true measure of their dedication; he has raised this before.

outline.heading: Gaza vanishes within weeks; Sudan starves
outline.gist: While the bombing lasts it is the only topic; three or four weeks after it stops it leaves public consciousness, as if things were back to normal, while Sudan starves. We get tired and want a break.

outline.heading: A personal break, not collective forgetting
outline.gist: Turning off the news to focus inward is healthy and prevents burnout, but it must not become the ummah's way of waiting for the issue to end. He charges his younger brothers and sisters to keep just causes alive for their generation.

outline.heading: Are the people of Gaza not tired?
outline.gist: Ignoring it until the bombing starts again is rinse and repeat; those under dictatorships do not get to tire of oppression. Change never comes quickly; it takes a generation or more, but it comes.

outline.heading: You don't have to be there for the fireworks
outline.gist: The Prophet died some thirty years before what his ummah became; Allah took him early to teach that you plant the seeds and dedicate your short time, as the founders of most movements in history never saw the result.

outline.heading: He promised Kisra's treasures to frightened people
outline.gist: In the midst of their suffering he promised the treasures of Kisra, the gates of al-Mada'in and the Roman castles, to people who could not even relieve themselves safely. He knew how change works; we heat up and cool down too fast.

outline.heading: The ten commandments of the Quran
outline.gist: These verses and the parallel passage in Al-An'am are called the Quran's ten commandments, as the Torah had its own; earlier scholars said everything of good in this world is placed in them.

outline.heading: Your Lord has decreed
outline.gist: He chooses passages scholars singled out. At his first lesson on these verses the teacher recited the opening words and spent the whole session on them: a decree is a judge's verdict.

outline.heading: Take it or leave it: His decree
outline.gist: People may say and do what they want, but this is His decision; a heart that knows the Almighty stops there and accepts whatever comes next. Your service and worship are for no one but Him.

outline.heading: None worthy but Him; then your parents
outline.gist: No one else can be seen as worthy of your worship; everyone is a distant second, a creation like you. Then comes excellence to both parents, especially if you live to see them grow old.

outline.heading: Not even uff
outline.gist: Once you have the upper hand and they are the ones in need, do not let even the sound of frustration out; you may feel it, just do not show it. Uff is not a word, only a sound built on the weakest letter.

outline.heading: Do not rebuke them; speak a noble word
outline.gist: Fa is the only Arabic letter with all five categories of weakness and none of strength. Do not chastise them for old mistakes you have not let go of; say something noble, because this is about your commitment to God.

outline.heading: No good for your parents, no good in you
outline.gist: Worship Him alone, and second, show your parents excellence; if you cannot care for those who cared for you, no amount of volunteering shows any good in you.

outline.heading: Lower the wing of humility
outline.gist: How will you worship the One who created you from nothing if you neglect those who fed and clothed you? Lower the wing of humility out of mercy; it is His decree and the speaker's job is only to convey it.

outline.heading: Have mercy on them as they raised me
outline.gist: The dua for parents; the verse speaks of parents who cared for you as a child, not those who abandoned you, and that is the majority of stories.

outline.heading: Your Lord knows what is in your hearts
outline.gist: You may feel mistreated or carry pain; He knows what happened. Do not worry about that piece, behave rightly, and He forgives those who keep returning.

outline.heading: The rights of relatives, the needy and the stranded
outline.gist: They have rights upon you, not by his opinion but by the Quran, because you owe Allah: you do not own the money, He does.

outline.heading: The wasteful are siblings of the devils
outline.gist: Do not waste what you were given. Shaytan's defining fault was ingratitude: lifted from the earth to live among the angels, he still refused to prostrate to Adam.

outline.heading: If you must leave them
outline.gist: If you have nothing to give, or must leave your parents and relatives behind to study, work or flee oppression in pursuit of your Lord's mercy, you cannot stay to serve them.

outline.heading: Neither a tight fist nor an open hand
outline.gist: Leave with kind words. Do not chain your hand to your neck or open it completely, or you will be blamed for hoarding or for waste and left with remorse.

outline.heading: Allah extends and restricts provision
outline.gist: He gives some abundance and holds back from others, and He knows His servants best. Out of time, he asks them to read the rest of the commands, which are profound.

outline.heading: As if these were your only verses
outline.gist: Imagine accepting Islam in Makkah, learning only these verses before being driven back to your tribe with Quraysh after you; living by them through verse 39 would be enough to live righteously.

outline.heading: Outro
